one_line_contribution: In ALFWorld, plant scene-specific procedure bindings (which of two identically-behaving appliances actually heats/cools/cleans) and cross that with whether a wrong choice is detectable before committing, to show that a per-instance lookup (scene-keyed retrieval, or an observation-keyed compiled table) is necessary only in the untestable regime, while in the testable regime a 60-token 'try it and switch' rule buys the same accuracy at zero uncached prefill.
closest_prior_work: The strongest threat I verified is LongMemEval-V2 (arXiv:2605.12493, 2026-05-12, verified via the literature command, S2+HF), which is built precisely around agents acquiring *environment-specific* experience and ships two memory methods that are the same contrast this proposal makes its headline: AgentRunbook-R, a RAG memory over raw state observations and strategy notes, versus AgentRunbook-C, which compiles trajectory-derived knowledge once, compared on accuracy *and* latency. That is retrieval-vs-compiled-artifact on instance-specific environment knowledge under a cost axis, i.e. the proposal's S2-vs-R3 comparison, already published four months ago and never cited here. It does not fully pre-empt: it does not plant the binding, does not manipulate whether the binding is probe-able at run time, and has no run-time-test rule arm, so the 'only when untestable' axis survives. Second, ScrambleToolBench (arXiv:2608.02358, 2026-08-03, verified, literature command) already benchmarks agents discovering hidden per-environment behaviors by interaction and reports they over-explore rather than use their own map, which is most of what P2 and P5 would find. Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv:2409.07429, verified) is the closest named compiled method and does not, as the proposal says, contain a probe or a bindings manipulation. Also verified: SGR-Bench 2605.22219, Mem2ActBench 2601.19935, SWE-ContextBench 2602.08316, 'When Agents Commit Too Soon' 2606.22936, ICAL 2406.14596, task-recognition-vs-task-learning 2305.09731, Preping 2605.13880 — all real and all described accurately. I did not individually verify the remaining IDs listed inside the proposal's own collision-check result lists (2609.04148, 2604.00356, 2512.01945, 2607.12397, 2501.01702, 2605.13511, 2506.04579, 2210.03821, 2608.10509, 2607.20999, 2603.21520, 2605.24117); several of them (2606.19911, 2608.07169, 2309.07900, 2202.12837) came back in my own searches and check out.
strongest_objection: The manipulated axis is not testability, it is testability confounded with irreversibility, and the proposal knowingly runs only the diagonal of the 2x2. 'Untestable' here means the wrong action returns a success string AND silently spends the procedure step AND cannot be undone; 'testable' means it returns 'Nothing happens' AND is free. Any interaction found is therefore equally explained by 'a query is needed when a mistake is unrecoverable' — a different and much older claim. The proposal names this in its limitations and then declines to run the third cell, which is exactly the cell that would identify the axis its title claims. Compounding this, the rule half of the headline interaction is definitional: the untestable regime is constructed so the probe rule can never receive its trigger, so D(S1, untestable) = D(S0, untestable) is an arithmetic consequence of the wrapper, not a result — which is precisely what Appendix B's 'no prediction entailed by a definition' rule forbids, and the automated entailment check flags the same thing. What is actually tested is the sufficiency half (can this reader use a retrieved name, or route a 30-row table), which is a Qwen3-32B competence measurement, not a law about when memory needs a query. A second, concrete objection: 'untestable' is untestable only against the one probe the experimenter chose. The wrapper hides the *procedure* response, but the receptacles' contents are explicitly not rewritten ('a fridge full of plates is a weak leak'), so `examine`/`open` remains a free, non-committing test of which appliance is which. That both contradicts the stated leak probe (which demands byte-identical strings for open/examine on both pair members) and means a reader with a slightly better rule — 'open both, act on the one that looks like a fridge' — would remove the penalty under 'untestable' with no memory at all, collapsing P3.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Run the 2x2 of {feedback signal present/absent} x {wrong attempt reversible/irreversible}, or at minimum add the undetectable-but-reversible cell that is currently cut; without it the title's causal variable is not identified. The cheap version: keep the untestable string but let the procedure step be retried, and add the 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' redundancy rule the proposal already describes as the answer there — if redundancy removes the penalty, the necessity claim is about irreversibility, not testability. (2) Resolve the leak contradiction: either rewrite receptacle contents so that no non-committing inspection distinguishes the pair (and re-run the leak probe on open/examine, reporting the strings), or drop the 'untestable' label and call the regime 'costly-to-test'. (3) Make P1's undefined 12-20 band a decision rule, and drop the TOST conjuncts in P2 and P4, which are implied by their companion '<= 12' claims plus the ~0 floor on D and so add no falsifiable content. (4) Fix P6: W-'s random other-kitchen item carries the correct binding half the time under q = .5, so W+ - W- estimates roughly half the locate-and-use effect against a 12-point margin; force W- to a kitchen with the opposite binding. (5) State the interaction as a pre-registered difference-in-differences with a power calculation, not as two separate '<= 12' bounds against a +-8 floor — a 12-point residual is a large effect to declare 'removed'.
missing_baseline: A no-memory inspection-probe arm under the untestable regime: a rule that uses free, non-committing actions (open/examine both appliances, or the redundancy rule 'do the step at both') rather than the procedure action itself. Under the plan as written, only the procedure action is silenced, so this arm can plausibly remove the swap penalty with zero retrieval and zero compiled binding — and if it does, P3's 'a per-instance lookup is necessary' is false as stated. A reviewer will ask for it because the proposal itself describes the redundancy rule and then declares its regime out of scope. Second omission: a retrieval placebo matched to W-, i.e. R3 with the three retrieved items forced to a kitchen carrying the opposite binding. R3o (oracle) bounds the retriever from above but nothing bounds it from below, so a positive R3 result cannot be attributed to the transferred binding rather than to generic same-type trajectory quality.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. My queries, all answered by channel (a), the literature command (S2 + HF); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Q1 'instance-specific bindings retrieved experience versus compiled static prompt LLM agent when is retrieval necessary' (no recency filter) returned memory-substrate and retrieval-vs-utilization work (2608.15008, 2603.02473, 2606.04315, 2605.11325) but nothing on a testability axis. Q2 'agent can probe environment feedback instead of remembering hidden per-scene parameter silent failure memory necessity' --recent returned 2601.04235 (agent actively obtains environmental feedback without predefined measurements), 2607.10608 (compliance trap), 2608.04574 (stale spatial memory), 2605.29463 — adjacent, none making the claim. Q3 'counterfactual perturbation of environment to test when episodic memory is necessary planted hidden task variable ALFWorld swap' --recent returned nothing on-topic (Preping 2605.13880 the closest). Q4, closest named method, 'Agent Workflow Memory induce reusable workflows from trajectories' returned AWM itself (2409.07429, verified, contra the proposal's claim that AWM 'was not returned'), plus 2605.12493, 2608.07169, 2606.19911. Q5 'trial and error at inference substitutes for memory when errors are recoverable irreversible actions require prior knowledge agent' --recent returned ScrambleToolBench 2608.02358 and 2607.29468. Q6, home literature, 'when do in-context demonstrations supply information that cannot be inferred from feedback latent variable identification' returned 2605.26350, 2309.07900, 2202.12837, 2406.14596 — none with a run-time-testability axis. Judging the proposal's own check: it is better than most — queries are quoted, classed, channel-labelled and given with IDs, and it correctly identifies 2606.22936 as the nearest diagnostic. But it has two holes and one misstatement. Hole 1: it ran no query on the retrieval-vs-compiled-runbook line and so missed LongMemEval-V2 (2605.12493, 2026-05), which is the single closest published comparison to its S2-vs-R3 arm and which sits squarely in its own topic. Hole 2: its 'home-vocabulary' queries went to in-context example selection, not to the literature that actually owns this claim — value of information / active exploration, where 'when does a probe substitute for prior knowledge' is a solved formalism; its own novelty card even surfaced 2604.24555 (bandits with side observations) via the adjacent query and the proposal ignored it. Misstatement: it reports that AWM 'itself not returned', which my identical-intent query contradicts — a check that reports an absence it cannot reproduce weakens the rest of it.
